newsitem.title: USA: Lower paper prices hurt R.R. Donnelley results.
newsitem.headline: Lower paper prices hurt R.R. Donnelley results.

text.p: Publishing giant R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co. said third-quarter profit and sales declined due to lower paper prices and other factors.
Donnelley said its earnings fell to $67.9 million, or 45 cents a share, from $92 million, or 60 cents a share, a year earlier.
Quarterly sales were down 6 percent, or $102 million, to $1.6 billion from the year-ago quarter, the company said.
"Lower paper prices resulted in a $133 million sales decline in the period," the company said, adding that volume gains in other businesses offset those declines.
Donnelley's shares were down 87.5 cents at $31.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
For the first nine months, Donnelley lost $255 million, or $1.66 a share, on sales of $4.73 billion, which compared with a profit of $203 million, $1.33 a share, on revenue of $4.51 billion.
The nine month results included a one-time restructuring charge of $560 million that was posted in the second quarter.
